summary.headline: Nisus standalone core revenue rose 110% YoY to INR 141 crore and PAT to INR 68 crore (48% margin) in FY26, with Q4 PAT of INR 11 crore.
summary.overview: FY26 was the first full year as a listed company, and management said core standalone revenue (ex-NCCCL) of INR 141 crore beat the INR 120-140 crore guidance despite a Q4 slowdown tied to West Asia conflict. Q4 core PAT was INR 11 crore, and the consolidated group (including NCCCL, acquired August 2025) reported revenue of INR 575 crore and PAT of INR 83 crore. Management said UAE transactions worth over INR 500 crore were deferred rather than lost, and FY27 guidance is presented as a two-scenario framework rather than a point estimate. NCCCL's PAT rose to INR 16.4 crore from INR 3.5 crore, and its order book was INR 1,833 crore at March-end, plus INR 870 crore added in April-May 2026.

financial_highlights.change: ~4.7x from INR 3.5 crore; NCCCL top line up ~7%

segments.name: Fund and asset management (core)
segments.commentary: Management said fund and asset management is now about 55% of core revenue versus advisory at about 45%; fee income is largely from sponsor capital in own funds plus treasury/investment income. UAE GCC portfolio of four assets reported 30% NAV growth in latest valuation, with management saying no impairment.

segments.name: Transaction advisory (core)
segments.commentary: Advisory held firm in Q4 despite the UAE transaction slowdown and was described as the counter-cyclical offset; advisory share was 67% of revenue when the business started versus about 55% now.

segments.name: NCCCL (construction/EPC, consolidated from Aug 2025)
segments.commentary: Order book INR 1,833 crore at 31 March 2026, plus INR 870 crore added in first two months of FY27 (management cites ~INR 2,600-2,700 crore total). Repaid about 65% of acquisition debt (INR 38 crore outstanding at March 31); EBITDA margin about 9%, PAT margin about 2-3%.

segments.name: Tokenisation (UAE)
segments.commentary: Presented as a separate digital asset business in the UAE entity; awaiting token issuance licence and white paper approval, with live launch hoped for within FY27. No financial contribution quantified.

guidance_outlook: FY27 core business: management referenced an EM (equity/assets under management) target of INR 4,500-5,000 crore; the Nisus Neon fund (INR 1,800 crore, INR 500 crore green shoe) received SEBI approval and launches from Q2 FY27, with fees broadly INR 220 crore.

FY27 revenue-to-AUM ratio assumed at around 2.85% (blended), with management calling 3% a steady-state assumption versus 5.3-5.6% in FY26, which included one-off UAE advisory contracts and book investment gains.
NCCCL FY27 target of about INR 850 crore revenue; management aims for 3-4x turnover over the next year per Vice Chairman, with EBITDA margins of 9-10%.
REIC Ops fund (launched 2019) expected to wind up in 2026, with management fee booking expected more likely in Q2 FY27.
Pipeline: India about INR 700 crore (60-70% at term sheet); UAE about INR 2,000 crore being renegotiated on entry prices; management expects India deployment over the next couple of quarters.
capex_capacity: Own prop book investment grew to about INR 2,125 crore (almost 4x), per management; a separate slide cited INR 48 crore to INR 128 crore growth for a different measure, so the figures should be verified against the presentation.

Two India transactions (about INR 150 crore each) slipped by a few months due to Pune land demarcation methodology change, lender committee NOC delays, and RERA/e-Khata issues in Gujarat, Karnataka and Telangana; management expects these to close in the current quarter.
UAE deferred deals: one INR 500 crore transaction and one INR 300 crore transaction pushed to later closure.
NCCCL migrating to SAP HANA and adopting digital project management tools.
demand_pricing: Dubai: off-plan share fell from about 78% last year to much smaller levels as ready-to-move-in inventory rose to about 60-70%; investor purchases fell from about 87% (2017-18) to about 45%, with end-users at about 55%.

Dubai pricing: management cited 10-15% discounts from January levels in Dubai and 5% in Abu Dhabi, with a weighted average market discount of roughly 15-20%; management said its own assets were up around 30% in valuation.
Management said it is buying at discounts to market and that renegotiation of entry prices is underway on the INR 2,000 crore UAE pipeline.
NCCCL works on 3-4 year order book visibility; industry EBITDA norm 9-10%, PAT 3-4%.
Management said advisory fees are directly correlated with AUM and fund size, and that the blended AUM-fee mix should shift toward management fees over time.

qa_highlights.question: What regulatory or lender-approval delays pushed India transactions out, and what is the status?
qa_highlights.answer: Avadhoot Sarwate said Pune demarcation methodology changed, and consortium lender NOCs took longer (March to May); about two trades of roughly INR 150 crore each slipped by a few months and are expected this quarter. Gujarat RERA and Bengaluru e-Khata were also cited as slowing approvals.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Neon Fund size, fees and timing, and REIC Ops closure economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Aanchal Singh said SEBI approval for the Neon Fund came the previous day, with launch from Q2; INR 1,800 crore fund plus INR 500 crore green shoe, fees broadly INR 220 crore, 7.5-year tenure. REIC Ops has a 12% hurdle with no catch-up, closing this year, with fees more likely in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the core run-rate fee income excluding one-time investment gains, and how does revenue compare to cost base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the segment reporting does not split recurring fees from treasury income; fee income is described as small relative to the fund and asset management segment, which includes treasury income from sponsor capital in own funds. No quantified run-rate was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 revenue-to-AUM assumed at 2.85% versus 5.3% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 was inflated by high-margin UAE advisory contracts and book investment gains on yield compression; 3% is the steady-state assumption, and capital is expected to deploy mainly in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the India (INR 700 crore) and UAE (INR 2,000 crore) pipelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Avadhoot Sarwate said 60-70% of the India pipeline is at term sheet stage, with deployment in the next couple of quarters. For UAE, management said 50-60% of the pipeline is at a complete stage, and at least INR 800 crore of transactions were deferred.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone employee costs rise to 32% of revenue, and what is the outlook for NCCCL margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited new hires, annual appraisals, and a change to accrual-based bonus accounting from this year. NCCCL margins target 9-10% EBITDA with 2-3% PAT, with growth coming from volume.

risks_watch: UAE real estate weakness: off-plan decline, lower investor demand, and deferrals of INR 500-800 crore deals; management did not give a timeline for stabilisation.
Approval and lender consortium delays in India (RERA, e-Khata, Pune demarcation) could keep pushing deployment into later quarters.
NCCCL execution: PAT margins of about 2-3%, dependence on order inflows, and a stated target of 3-4x revenue next year.
Revenue-to-AUM ratio step-down from 5.3% to about 2.85% in FY27 guidance; one-off gains in FY26 will not recur in the base.
Stock price weakness since IPO (~50% down per an investor question); management attributed this to market perception rather than fundamentals.
Tokenisation and Neon fund launches depend on regulatory approvals (token licence and white paper; SEBI approved Neon fund).
summary.management_tone: Confident on reported FY26 numbers and the balance sheet, but cautious on the forward outlook, with management repeatedly citing West Asia conflict and calibrated deployment. Management was defensive and sometimes evasive on the share price and on the split of recurring fee income, and it deferred to the presentation for segment detail.
key_quotes: The key point is that the question is timing, not structural.
caution and conservative approach with capital protection is the name of the game.
Our core business of Q4 delivered a PAT of INR 11 crores, healthy margins across EBITDA, PAT and returns.
The order book is all about execute orders which are in hand of the company, okay?
